stories.headline: Mets' Cionel Perez: Reinstated from IL
stories.detail: The Mets reinstated Perez (forearm) from the injured list Saturday. A left forearm strain has kept Perez out of action since July 31, but he's now been cleared to return to the Mets' bullpen after firing four shutout innings in four rehab outings in the minors. He'll replace Cameron Weston on the active roster and will likely work in middle relief after turning in a 4.97 ERA across 41.2 frames while healthy.

stories.headline: Mets' Cameron Weston: Back in Triple-A
stories.detail: The Mets optioned Weston to Triple-A Syracuse on Saturday. The Mets brought Weston up from Triple-A on Thursday, but he'll now head back down to the minors without appearing in a game. Cionel Perez (forearm) was activated from the injured list to fill the open spot in New York's bullpen.

stories.headline: Orioles' Cade Povich: Sent down to Norfolk
stories.detail: The Orioles optioned Povich to Triple-A Norfolk on Saturday, Jake Rill of MLB.com reports. After giving up three earned runs in just 3.2 innings during his start against the Brewers on Friday, Povich will be sent back down to Triple-A to make room for Felix Bautista (shoulder), who returned from the 60-day IL on Saturday. Unless Povich returns to Baltimore as an injury replacement, he will finish the 2026 campaign with a 4.38 ERA, 1.49 WHIP and 28:15 K:BB across 37 MLB innings.

stories.headline: Rays' Taylor Walls: Sitting down Saturday
stories.detail: Walls isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against Boston, Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times reports. Walls will move to the bench after going 1-for-4 with two walks, two RBI and a run scored during his first two games back from the IL. Jorge Mateo will pick up a start at shortstop and bat ninth.

stories.headline: Rays' Yandy Diaz: Scratched Saturday
stories.detail: Diaz was scratched from the lineup for Saturday's game against the Red Sox, Ryan Bass of Rays .tv reports. It's unclear why the Rays took Diaz out of the starting nine Saturday, but the team should provide more information in the near future. In the meantime, Jake Fraley will fill in as Tampa Bay's designated hitter and bat leadoff.

stories.headline: Orioles' Felix Bautista: Returns from injured list
stories.detail: The Orioles reinstated Bautista (shoulder) from the 60-day injured list Saturday, Andy Kostka of TheBanner.com reports. Bautista will join the active roster for the first time since July 2025 after undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum and rotator cuff in his right shoulder. He was cleared to begin a rehab assignment Aug. 23 and has since given up five earned runs in eight innings while striking out nine batters and walking seven. The 31-year-old has consistently been one of Baltimore's most reliable high-leverage relievers throughout his career, but he may not step into a closing role immediately upon being activated due to the length of his absence and his subpar minor-league performance.

stories.headline: Orioles' Ryan Helsley: Shut down for season
stories.detail: President of baseball operations Mike Elias said Saturday that Helsley (elbow) will be shut down for the remainder of the season, Andy Kostka of TheBanner.com reports. Helsley has been working his way back from right elbow inflammation that forced him onto the injured list in late June, but he hasn't pitched in a rehab game at Triple-A Norfolk since last Saturday. With his progress stalling, the Orioles have officially now shifted their focus to getting the 32-year-old ready for 2027. He'll finish 2026 with a 4.11 ERA and 1.43 WHIP alongside a 21:9 K:BB across 15.1 innings.

stories.headline: Giants' Sam Hentges: Throws scoreless inning in rehab game
stories.detail: Hentges (forearm) threw a scoreless inning while striking out two in Triple-A Sacramento's 6-4 loss to Reno on Friday. Hentges was placed on the 15-day injured list Aug. 30 (retroactive to Aug. 27) due to a left forearm strain. The southpaw began a rehab assignment with Sacramento on Friday, throwing nine of his 14 pitches for strikes. He's running out of time to return to the big leagues this season, as San Francisco has already been eliminated from postseason contention.

stories.headline: Yankees' Max Schuemann: Joins big club
stories.detail: The Yankees recalled Schuemann from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre on Saturday. Schuemann has slashed .275/.333/.507 with three homers, six RBI and 14 runs scored across 76 plate appearances since being sent down to Triple-A in late August. He'll now return to the majors to give the Yankees a bench option capable of playing almost anywhere in the field while Aaron Judge (calf) is on the injured list.

stories.headline: Yankees' Aaron Judge: Move to IL official
stories.detail: The Yankees placed Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a right calf strain, retroactive to Thursday. Judge will be eligible to return from the injured list before New York's regular-season finale, though it's more likely that the team keeps him on the shelf until the postseason. Heliot Ramos is the favorite to take over as the Yankees' primary right fielder while Judge is out, and Max Schuemann will come up from Triple-A to fill the open roster spot.
